claims.quote: Synaptic accumulation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) oligomers and their interactions with VAMP2 have been reported to be the basis of synaptic dysfunction in Parkinson's disease (PD).
α-Syn mutants associated with familial PD have also been known to be capable of interacting with VAMP2,
A30P and A53T oligomers cluster vesicles in the presence of VAMP2,
E46K oligomers reduce the membrane mobility of the planar bilayers, as revealed by single-particle tracking, and permeabilize the membranes in the presence of VAMP2.
In the absence of VAMP2 interactions, E46K oligomers enlarge vesicles by fusing with one another.
